It's a great game and I enjoy it thoroughly, even as its auto-saving at weirdest checkpoints is trying really hard to make it the worst experience. How many times does one have to repeat 5, 10, 15 minutes of gameplay for it to become fun?
There are also some clunky controls and at times strangest movement. Apparently, you can easily step over many things but only if they are arranged in steps. If there's a nail sticking out of the flat ground, you'll likely have to jump over it. You can also climb a bit, but only a bit.
The enemies see through walls at times, and, perhaps, even shoot through walls, but this may be my imagination playing up.
Overall, the Exodus is a highly enjoyable experience. Especially if you can do everything in one go without having to rely on the abhorrent checkpoints.

Game launches you into a breathtaking, deadly world beyond the Metro. This is no ordinary shooter it's a story-driven survival epic wrapped in beauty, brutality, and hope. From frozen wastelands to sun-scorched deserts, every inch of the journey is drenched in atmosphere and consequence. Artyom’s quest for a new life is as emotional as it is explosive, and the open-world design never sacrifices tension or storytelling.

Another great game from a fantastic series. I will say that it is very different. The game play is not nearly as good as the previous titles but what it lakes in game play it more then makes up for it with story. The story is really well done, even if the ending depends on whether you were stealthy or not. It isn't the best game of all time but it's a lot of fun and still a must play. If you enjoy Russian based games as much as I do, then you'll absolutely love this game. I just hope the next Stalker game is really, really amazing as I can't imagine them making another Metro game.

Functionally, this is the most impressive of the Metro series and has a genuinely fun open world style of gameplay. Story wise, it pisses on the existing lore(which the fact that this one is 'inspired by' instead of 'based on' the books should tell you plenty). It actually hurts how much they twisted the story to create the drive for a lot of the early game. Those one-off characters from 2033 and Last Light trying to reach other parts of the world? Well now that's Artyom who has been doing it so much that his blood practically glows now. Why has nobody reached the outer world? Hanza has a jammer system in place that you accidentally discover and shoot. Not gonna get into the rest of the story shit because it's past the first ~10 minutes.
TL;DR: Great gameplay hindered by piss poor story......also there's the Enhanced Edition that will tell you to fuck off if you don't have an RTX card.

Based on a series of novels by Russian author Dmitry Glukhovsky, the first two Metro games were set in and around the Moscow metro system, where a small group of people have survived the outbreak of World War 3 and try to make a life in the tunnels/metro while avoiding the nuclear fallout above ground.

Metro Exodus is 3rd installment in the series and for now is best post-apocalyptic survival game of the generation. The mix of linear and open world areas works really good, with constant rewards for exploration. Morality system and thought-provoking parts of the game make this game really unique. While developer 4A Games has put a lot of effort into Metro Exodus' weapons, it has also crafted a game world where stealth is a really viable option. Most of the action takes place on the surface of post-apocalyptic Russia rather than its underground makin a really great change.

Graphics and world design are 10/10 for me atleast, especially design of this beatiful post apocalyptic wasteland. As a big fan of S.T.A.L.K.E.R and Fallout series I highly recommend this game. Real masterpiece

An extremely well-crafted game with beautiful graphics and excellent gameplay. Whether you're a stealthy stalker or you "just start blastin'", you can approach the missions whichever way you want. Fans of the horror genre will also get their share of jump scares and creepy locales. It's not often these days that a first-person shooter has relatable characters you actually enjoy interacting with outside of combat, so it was refreshing to blaze a trail through Russia with this ragtag crew. The two DLCs are just as packed with story and action as the main storyline, so definitely check those out as well. 

This was my first exodus into the world of Metro, and this game certainly makes me want to check out the other earlier games in the series as well as the much-lauded book!

Metro Exodus is the third game in the Metro series and represents the biggest leap forward.

Graphically, the game is a 10/10. It's fantastic. There's no comparison to its already visually appealing predecessors. The story once again surpasses its predecessors and casts them into shadow. Exciting, incredibly immersive, and extremely emotional, it's one of the few games that brought tears to my eyes. It's a journey that everyone should experience at least once.

However, the gameplay differs from its predecessors and might deter some old fans. There are now small open-world or rather open maps. These are extremely well-crafted, highly detailed, and offer a lot to do. The beauty of it is that there are no unnecessary side missions; there's no simple checklist to complete, and the story unfolds beautifully within those areas. At the same time, there are still plenty of tight and horror-like passages that target the hearts of old players.

Metro Exodus is a game that shouldn't just be played through; it should be savored and experienced. There are so many beautiful dialogues and details that the game thrives on exploration and soaking up as much as possible. The replay value is also much greater than in its predecessors.

For me, the game is a 10/10 and my all-time favorite game. I can only recommend that everyone experiences the pinnacle of the Metro series for themselves. Play it, and you won't regret it.

I really wanted to like this game. It is true that it kinda - sorta - scratches that old Stalker itch, but mostly in the sense of being full of bugs and glitches. In addition to several weird graphical glitches like black screen while the game is playing, refusing to let me tab out of the game, eternally spinning blue circles instead of a cursor etc -- there were also really annoying glitches like monsters glitching through doors and glitching into the air and other glitches that diminish the fun of the game. In the final analysis, this game reminded me more of Fallout 76 than the Stalkers. And just as Fallout 76 turned out to NOT be fun, I didn't find Exodus to really be fun. It seemed more tedious than fun. To be fair, I didn't really like the first two Metro games, so I shouldn't have fallen for the "its the best thing since Stalker" hype. Trust me, its not.

Great end ? to a great series. While the character movement is weird and janky at times, gunplay is superb, exploration is fun, and it generally holds together much of what made the earlier games good without upending everything. A more open form of gameplay really helps spice things up while still keeping the majority of linearity. That said; I genuinely never understood Anna in the game she premiered in and seemed like an afterthought created to give Artyom a romantic interest, that is largely fixed in this game despite using her less interesting personality but develops it into being a more whole character.

Overall an amazing game that made me cry, is worth playing even if you're not a fan of the earlier Metro games.

I don't agree with the epic store exclusive nonsense but I'll just focus on the game...The graphics and atmosphere are top notch and really pulled me into the world and story of Metro. The story continues on from the previous games but I think you can play this one without playing the previous entries. The gunplay, open world and crafting systems are all quite good, I've encountered some bugs and poor FPS drops but nothing that would turn me off from the game.

If this series is to continue I hope to never see it an epic exclusive again.
